note: Engineering draft. Every rule needs clinical review before release. A relationship here is an association or a contrast. It is never a cause.

scenario_rules.interpretation: Your blood results and your predicted risk both point to this area. They measure different things, and one has not been shown to cause the other.
scenario_rules.rationale: Measured results and a model prediction are separate kinds of evidence that agree in direction. No causal link is established.

scenario_rules.interpretation: Your blood results are outside range, but your predicted risk is not raised. A lower predicted risk does not cancel results that are outside range.
scenario_rules.rationale: The two measure different things. A prediction does not correct a measurement.

scenario_rules.interpretation: Your blood results are within range, but your assessment flags an increased predicted risk. Results in range do not rule out a predicted risk.
scenario_rules.rationale: A prediction can use more than the blood results, and a result in range is one reading.

scenario_rules.interpretation: Your blood results and your predicted risk are both encouraging for this area. That does not mean you are risk free.
scenario_rules.rationale: Both sources agree in direction. Neither rules out future problems.

marker_group_rules.interpretation: More than one of your blood sugar results is outside range. They are read together: HbA1c reflects your average over a few months, and fasting sugar is one morning.
marker_group_rules.rationale: Related glucose measures are interpreted as one pattern. The wording does not name a condition.

marker_group_rules.interpretation: More than one of your cholesterol and blood fat results is outside range. They are read together, as one picture of your blood fats.
marker_group_rules.rationale: Lipid measures are interpreted as a set. The wording does not name a condition.

lifestyle_rules.interpretation: Your HDL cholesterol is below your laboratory's reference range, and you have reported low physical activity. Regular physical activity can support cardiovascular health and healthier cholesterol patterns. This does not mean that low activity caused your HDL result.
lifestyle_rules.rationale: Physical activity is a recognised influence on HDL. The wording states an association and no cause.

lifestyle_rules.interpretation: Your HDL cholesterol is below your laboratory's reference range even though you have reported being physically active. Activity is only one thing that can influence HDL. Genetics, smoking, body weight and the fats in your diet can also play a part, so it is worth discussing the whole picture with your doctor.
lifestyle_rules.rationale: Activity alone does not explain HDL. The wording avoids repeating beginner advice and names other influences.

lifestyle_rules.interpretation: Your triglycerides are above your laboratory's reference range, and you have reported low physical activity. Regular activity can support healthier triglyceride levels. This does not mean that low activity caused this result.
lifestyle_rules.rationale: Physical activity is a recognised influence on triglycerides. The wording states an association and no cause.

lifestyle_rules.interpretation: Your LDL related cholesterol is above your laboratory's reference range, and you have reported low physical activity. Activity is one of several things that can influence cholesterol, along with diet and genetics. This does not mean that low activity caused this result.
lifestyle_rules.rationale: Physical activity is one of several recognised influences. The wording states an association and no cause.
